subject: PayFlux SDK: endpoint migration, retries/timeouts, and rate-limit plan
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@payflux.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PayFlux SDK migration questions (endpoints, retries, rate limits)

Hi Priyom / Monica,

Thanks for picking this up. We're starting an effort to migrate our production integrations from a self-hosted endpoint to Redwood's hosted SDK endpoints. A few things we need clarity on before the kickoff: 

- Sample code: do you have a minimal Node/Python sample that shows SDK setup, token refresh and env var patterns?
- Endpoint migration: recommended cutover approach (dark launch, canary %, time windows). We're currently sending ~800 req/min with occasional 95th percentile spikes to 1.1k req/min.
- Retries & timeouts: what's Redwood's recommended client-side strategy for 429/504/500; do we honor Retry-After?
- Rate limits: how aggressive should client rate limiting be, and do you expose headers for remaining quota?

Attached: payflux_current_config.yaml (current routing config), sample_logs.txt (3-day window showing spikes).

Goal: get a practical step-by-step we can hand to our infra team and schedule a short kickoff this week.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, PayFlux

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@payflux.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PayFlux SDK migration questions (endpoints, retries, rate limits)

Hi Samira — thanks for the context and attachments. High-level plan below; I'll share a short starter repo and an integration checklist as well.

Quick plan (practical):
1) Sandbox validation (0-2 days)
   - Give you a sandbox key and a short Node + Python example that mirrors your traffic pattern.
   - Run synthetic load to validate token refresh and KV/cache behavior.

2) SDK setup (1 day)
   - Install: npm i @redwood/sdk or pip install redwood-sdk
   - Env: REDWOOD_API_KEY (scoped, rotate in 30 days), REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox/prod
   - Minimal Node example (pseudo):
     const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
     const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, timeoutMs: 8000 });
     
     // call with simple retry wrapper shown in repo

3) Endpoint migration strategy (canary + gradual shift)
   - Phase A (Dark launch): send duplicated requests to Redwood endpoint (no production user impact) for 24–48h. Monitor latency and errors.
   - Phase B (Canary): route 5–10% of traffic for 2–4 hours, then 25% for 4–8 hours, then 50/75/100.
   - If error rate or 95th latency exceeds your threshold, automatic rollback to previous provider.

4) Retries & timeouts (recommended)
   - Client timeouts: connect 1.5s, read 8s (increase for long-completions).
   - Retry policy: idempotent requests: exponential backoff with full jitter (initial 200ms, factor 2, max cap 5s, max attempts 5).
   - For 429: respect Retry-After if present; otherwise use backoff + jitter and reduce concurrency.
   - For 500/502/504: retry with backoff but increment a circuit-breaker counter — fail fast after 5 consecutive failures for 30s.

5) Rate limiting guidance
   - Given your observed 95th spikes ~1.1k/min, client-side token-bucket limiter set to 1,000 req/min with a burst bucket of 200 handles short spikes; Redwood's gateway also returns X-RateLimit-* headers.
   - We'll surface remaining quota header as X-Redwood-Remaining (you'll see it in sandbox).

6) Observability & rollback
   - Add a short health-check endpoint on your side to detect increased 5xx/latency and automate traffic rollback.

I'll attach the integration-checklist.xlsx and push a minimal examples branch to the repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/example-sdk-integration/tree/payflux.

Propose a 30-minute kickoff at 10:30 AM PT today if that works — we can walk the repo and map responsibilities.

Attaching: integration-checklist.xlsx

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PayFlux SDK migration questions (endpoints, retries, rate limits)

Samira — quick account context and next steps from CS: 

- Account pulse: PayFlux is on our Growth tier with reserved burst allowances; your committed baseline is 600 req/min with burst headroom (we monitor).
- Recommended client-side settings (summary): 1,000 req/min steady, burst 200; 5 retry attempts max; honor Retry-After for 429.
- SLA notes: we'll provide 99.5% gateway availability during business hours; any extended degradations trigger an SRE incident and the rollback policy Priyom outlined.

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood (Priyom): share starter repo + checklist (done) and demo sandbox.
- PayFlux (Samira/Integration Team): run sandbox validation tests, share failing traces if any.
- CS (Monica): coordinate kickoff, MRR/usage tracking, and MAP update.

I've attached the first draft of the mutual action plan (PayFlux_MAP_v1.docx). I've also penciled the kickoff for 10:30 AM PT — Priyom, Vivek: can you confirm?

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that looks good. Confirming 10:30 AM PT works for us. A couple of quick clarifications before the call: 

> From: Priyom Das
> "Retry policy: idempotent requests: exponential backoff with full jitter (initial 200ms, factor 2, max cap 5s, max attempts 5)."

1) For non-idempotent requests (writes), do you recommend using a dedup token + a shortened retry window? If so, what's the suggested TTL for dedup tokens?
2) Does the Redwood SDK automatically surface Retry-After and implement the backoff for you, or do we need to add the wrapper in our service?

We'll bring these two items to the kickoff. Looking forward to the repo link — I couldn't access the Drive yet (permission request sent).

Best,
Samira
Head of Integrations, PayFlux
